subject: general
question: Epic Poem, Savitri, described by its author as 'A Legend and a Symbol', was written by _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurobindo Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Epic Poem Savitri** is considered one of the greatest works of **Sri Aurobindo Ghosh**, often described as a spiritual and philosophical masterpiece.
 
• Sri Aurobindo referred to **Savitri** as "A Legend and a Symbol," which is a reflective interpretation of the eternal human quest for spiritual realization.
 
• The poem is composed of **12 books and 49 cantos**, covering over 23,000 lines, making it one of the longest epic poems in English literature.
 
• It is based on the **mythological story of Savitri and Satyavan** from the Mahabharata, reinterpreted as a metaphor for the transformation of human consciousness.
 
• The work encapsulates Sri Aurobindo's vision of the Divine Life on Earth and is deeply rooted in his philosophy of Integral Yoga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sri Aurobindo Ghosh** (1872–1950) was a philosopher, poet, nationalist, and spiritual reformer who played a significant role in India's independence movement before dedicating his life to spiritual pursuits.
 
• His philosophy of **Integral Yoga** emphasizes the synthesis of physical, mental, and spiritual evolution to create a divine life on Earth.
 
• The story of Savitri and Satyavan from the Mahabharata symbolizes **human resilience, devotion, and the conquest of death through love and divine intervention.**
 
• Sri Aurobindo's poetic style in Savitri is marked by its spiritual depth, symbolic imagery, and philosophical insights, making it a unique contribution to world literature.
 
• His works, including **The Life Divine**, **Essays on the Gita**, and **Savitri**, reflect his vision of spiritual evolution and the integration of the material and spiritual worlds.
